standard_prerequisites.name: Extension of the vanishing from coherent to quasi-coherent modules by filtered colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-directed-colimit-coherent and lemma-colimits (invoked at proof line 3223)
standard_prerequisites.use: They upgrade the hypothesis $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for coherent $\mathcal{F}$ to the same vanishing for every quasi-coherent module.

standard_prerequisites.name: Serre's criterion for affineness in the vanishing situation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label proposition-vanishing-affine (invoked at proof line 3225)
standard_prerequisites.use: Once the vanishing holds for all quasi-coherent modules, it gives that $X$ is an affine scheme.

core_obligations: Use the colimit description of quasi-coherent modules and the commutation of cohomology with filtered colimits to extend the vanishing hypothesis to all quasi-coherent modules (proof lines 3221-3223).
Apply Serre's criterion for affineness to conclude that $X$ is an affine scheme (proof lines 3224-3225).
difficulty_reason: The lemma deduces affineness of a Noetherian algebraic space from the vanishing of the first cohomology of all coherent modules (statement lines 3212-3218). The proof extends the vanishing to quasi-coherent modules by writing them as filtered colimits of coherent ones, and then applies Serre's criterion for affineness. The extension step through the colimit lemmas is the substance, so the claim is H2.
